strengths: The paper addresses an important deployment problem in cooperative perception and is best assessed as an Applied/Systems contribution: it jointly targets model inference, communication, and memory rather than optimizing detection accuracy alone.

The proposed system combines end-to-end weight/activation quantization with codebook-based feature transmission, producing a substantial reported latency reduction from 127.7 ms to 40.0 ms while retaining near-full-precision accuracy for the main Pyramid Fusion configuration.

Evaluation covers three datasets, heterogeneous sensor/backbone settings, six fusion methods, pose perturbations, calibration sensitivity, power consumption, and comparisons with communication-efficient and PTQ baselines.

The results expose useful architecture-dependent behavior: CNN-based fusion is comparatively quantization-friendly, whereas V2X-ViT is highly sensitive. The paper appropriately acknowledges this limitation.
The manuscript is generally organized and includes component studies, latency breakdowns, message sizes, and implementation information that make the practical motivation easy to understand.
weaknesses: The central real-world deployment claim is not adequately supported. Computation is profiled on a desktop RTX 3090, while communication delay and asynchrony are simulated using a fixed 27 Mbps rate and a uniform 0–200 ms delay. There is no end-to-end over-the-air C-V2X evaluation, edge-device latency measurement, or distributional reporting across network conditions.

Important technical definitions are incorrect or incomplete. Equation 6 defines the quantization scale using only the integer range and bit width, omitting the observed floating-point range. The communication-volume expressions apply a logarithm to the total byte count instead of computing bytes/bits directly. These errors undermine the formal presentation of two central mechanisms.

The codebook mechanism is insufficiently specified. Equation 2 requires combination weights alpha, but the paper does not explain how they are obtained at the receiver or whether they are transmitted; their communication cost is omitted. The text also invokes product quantization without defining subspaces, and key quantities such as feature dimensions and complete encoding/decoding cost are absent.

Evidence for the alignment module is limited. The cumulative ablation does not independently isolate the heterogeneity and spatial losses, KL divergence over unnormalized feature tensors is not defined, and the spatial loss is simply output distillation without a clear mechanism connecting it to robustness against pose error or latency. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run statistics are reported.

The claimed generality is overstated: at 4/8 bits, V2X-ViT collapses from 57.4/49.5 to 29.9/8.8 AP30/50, and F-Cooper also degrades substantially. Most favorable system experiments use only PointPillar with Pyramid Fusion, limiting evidence for a broadly deployable multi-modal, multi-agent system.

The system comparison leaves confounders. QuantV2X is compared against methods with different message compressors and compute characteristics, but there is no controlled factorial study separating the accuracy effects of PTQ, codebook compression, reduced computation latency, and message latency. The mapping from sampled latency to dataset frames and final AP is also underdescribed.

The scalability claim rests mainly on a small plot without backbone identities, measured memory footprints, numerical results, or hardware-specific feasibility evidence. Reproducibility is further limited by unspecified calibration/search hyperparameters, loss weights, quantization granularity, and unavailable custom TensorRT/CUDA plug-ins; the promised release link is blank.

strengths: The paper targets an important practical problem: reducing both inference and communication costs in cooperative V2X perception. I assess it primarily as an Applied/Systems contribution rather than Algorithms/General, because its central claims concern deployability, latency, memory, and bandwidth.

Combining network quantization with compressed inter-agent messages is a sensible full-stack direction. On Pyramid Fusion, the reported INT4-weight/INT8-activation results retain much of the full-precision accuracy across DAIR-V2X, V2X-Real, and OPV2V.

The evaluation covers multiple datasets and fusion architectures and includes component, calibration-size, calibration-step, pose-noise, latency, and codebook-size studies. The comparison against CodeFilling is particularly relevant.
The manuscript is generally organized and acknowledges an important limitation: transformer-based V2X-ViT is not robust to the proposed aggressive quantization.
weaknesses: The communication formulation is technically incomplete and contains an apparent dimensional error. The manuscript defines message bandwidth as the logarithm of the total number of bytes, rather than the number of transmitted bits or bytes. Moreover, Eq. (2) reconstructs features using weights alpha_r, but the paper says that only code indices are transmitted and neither explains how these weights are recovered nor includes their cost. The claimed product quantization, nC parameter, codebook storage, index-search cost, and encoding/decoding latency are also insufficiently defined.

Core quantization and alignment details are not technically rigorous. Eq. (6) appears to confuse tensor extrema with integer quantization bounds, and the calibration range is later written in reversed order as [Xmax, Xmin]. KL divergence is applied directly to unspecified BEV feature tensors, although such tensors are not probability distributions. The L2 loss between predicted bounding-box representations does not specify matching, ordering, normalization, or handling of variable detection counts. Consequently, the claimed correction of heterogeneity and spatial misalignment is not reproducible or convincingly justified.

The headline real-world system claim is stronger than the evidence. The accuracy under latency is produced by simulating communication delay and a uniform 0–200 ms asynchronous offset on an offline dataset. Inference latency is averaged over only ten runs on an RTX 3090, not demonstrated on a constrained automotive device or an actual C-V2X network; the conclusion itself leaves real C-V2X testbed deployment to future work. There are no confidence intervals, packet-loss experiments, contention measurements, tail latency, warm-up protocol, or real temporal traces.

Reported efficiency numbers are internally difficult to reconcile. The model latencies of 59.5 ms and 27.1 ms imply throughputs far below the separately reported 47.6 and 124 QPS, yet the power table does not explain which workload or measurement boundary it uses. The custom TensorRT/CUDA implementation is not described sufficiently to determine whether precision modes and baselines received comparable optimization.

The advertised +9.5 mAP30 gain is mainly relative to an uncompressed 8.6 MB full-precision baseline under the simulated latency model. Against the much more relevant CodeFilling baseline at the same reported 0.03 MB message size, the improvement is only 1.2 mAP30. There is no clean system-level factorial ablation separating gains from model quantization, codebook transmission, alignment losses, and different effective staleness.

The novelty is limited: the system largely combines established ingredients—AdaRound-style rounding, block-wise PTQ reconstruction, feature distillation losses, and CodeFilling-like codebook communication. The paper does not clearly establish which technically new element, beyond their integration, accounts for the reported system gains.

The claim that the method generalizes across fusion architectures is contradicted by V2X-ViT, whose AP50 falls from 49.5 to 8.8 at INT4/INT8. Other architectures also incur notable losses. Most detailed evidence centers on Pyramid Fusion, and comparisons with modern PTQ methods are limited to one DAIR-V2X configuration.

The scaling experiment is too underspecified to support its conclusion. It does not report backbone identities, parameter counts, measured peak memory, allocation rules, or numerical results for each budget. Likewise, important reproducibility details are missing, including several loss/search hyperparameters, codebook weight generation, calibration sampling protocol, seeds, kernel specifications, and a concrete release link.

For a safety-relevant deployment paper, evaluation under distribution shift, weather, packet loss, bandwidth variation, calibration drift, rare objects, and detection distance/size strata is absent. These omissions materially weaken the claim of practical viability rather than merely representing optional extensions. strengths: Best assessed as an Applied/Systems contribution rather than the default Algorithms/General category: its main value is the full-stack integration of model quantization, codebook-based communication, TensorRT deployment, and resource-aware evaluation for cooperative perception.

The paper addresses an important practical gap in V2X perception. Quantizing the encoder, fusion module, detection head, and transmitted representation together is a useful systems direction beyond work that optimizes only communication or isolated network components.

The empirical scope is broad: three datasets, heterogeneous LiDAR/camera configurations, six fusion methods, INT8 and INT4/INT8 settings, pose-error robustness, calibration ablations, PTQ comparisons, latency, memory scaling, and energy measurements. Pyramid Fusion retains 74.2/66.7 AP30/50 versus 75.1/68.2 in FP32 at INT4/8, while V2X-Real and OPV2V also show small accuracy losses.

Deployment-oriented results are promising. The reported latency falls from 127.7 ms to 40.0 ms in the end-to-end breakdown, and QuantV2X obtains 52.6/42.2 system-level mAP30/50 on V2X-Real, close to the ideal upper bound of 53.8/43.5 and above CodeFilling's 51.4/40.8.

The component study provides evidence that heterogeneity and spatial alignment losses improve recovery over basic calibration, while the comparison against LiDAR-PTQ suggests a favorable accuracy/calibration-cost trade-off. The paper also acknowledges the substantial degradation of transformer-based fusion architectures rather than concealing this limitation.
weaknesses: Several central technical details are insufficiently or incorrectly specified. The communication-volume expressions take the logarithm of a byte count rather than computing the number of transmitted bits or bytes. The method alternates among nL, nC, and product-quantized codebooks without defining their relationship, and Eq. 2 uses combination weights alpha_r without explaining how the receiver obtains them when only indices are transmitted.

The quantization description contains ambiguities that hinder reproducibility: Eq. 6 appears to use quantized limits where the real-valued tensor range is required; the text reverses the range as [Xmax, Xmin]; granularity, signedness, per-channel versus per-tensor choices, handling of unsupported operators, and the exact integer execution path are not documented. Consequently, the claim of a fully quantized end-to-end system is difficult to verify.

The system evaluation needs a more auditable latency protocol. Figure 5 reports 127.7 ms and 40.0 ms totals, whereas Table 6 reports 59.5 ms and 27.1 ms, and the relationship between these measurements is not clearly explained. Moreover, the stated communication model Tcomm=fs/v+U(0,200) at 27 Mbps does not obviously agree with the plotted transmission latencies for the listed payload sizes. The paper should provide units, serialization assumptions, network stack details, and a complete per-baseline breakdown.

The headline system-level accuracy gains are produced by simulating latency on V2X-Real rather than by an end-to-end live V2X evaluation. The manuscript does not adequately explain how sampled delays are converted into temporally mismatched dataset observations, how many delay draws are used, or whether all methods receive identical draws. Results over multiple seeds with uncertainty would materially strengthen the evidence.

The alignment formulation is underspecified: KL divergence is applied to feature maps without defining normalization into probability distributions, and the L2 loss between predicted box representations does not explain matching, confidence treatment, or parameterization. Calling this an alignment 'module' is also confusing because it appears to consist primarily of calibration losses rather than a deployed architectural component.

Some deployment and scalability claims overreach the evidence. Profiling uses only ten runs on an RTX 3090, while the discussion targets constrained in-vehicle GPUs; Figure 6 lacks backbone identities and detailed memory measurements; and no comparisons are provided on representative embedded accelerators. The promised public release also has no accessible URL in the manuscript. These concerns prevent a stronger accept despite the promising applied contribution.

strengths: Although no contribution type is declared, the work is best assessed as Applied/Systems rather than the default Algorithms/General: its principal value is the end-to-end integration and deployment evaluation of model and message quantization, not a fundamentally new quantization algorithm. Under this framing, addressing computation, communication, and memory jointly is relevant and potentially impactful for cooperative perception.

QuantV2X presents a coherent full-stack design: end-to-end weight/activation quantization, codebook-index communication, and calibration losses intended to preserve heterogeneous and spatial features. The reported reduction from 127.7 ms to 40.0 ms, together with a much smaller 0.03 MB message, is practically meaningful.

The evaluation covers DAIR-V2X, V2X-Real, OPV2V, and V2X-ReaLO; multiple sensor/backbone configurations; and six fusion methods. Model-level results are strong for several architectures, with Pyramid Fusion retaining 74.2/66.7 AP30/50 at INT4/INT8 versus 75.1/68.2 in full precision.

The component studies examine calibration-set size, calibration steps, codebook configurations, pose noise, distance-dependent accuracy, and the respective effects of AdaRound and the proposed alignment losses. The online V2X-ReaLO results across V2V, I2I, and V2I modes add useful evidence beyond static benchmarks.
weaknesses: The central deployment claim is not yet supported with sufficient rigor. Main-paper system accuracy uses measured inference latency but a modeled communication delay at a fixed 27 Mbps plus sampled asynchrony. The V2X-ReaLO experiment provides online accuracy but no corresponding latency, hardware, bandwidth, sequence count, variability, or statistical uncertainty. Main latency numbers are averaged over only 10 runs on an RTX 3090, which is not representative of the constrained in-vehicle hardware emphasized in the motivation.

Baseline control is insufficiently documented. It is unclear whether CodeFilling and other communication baselines receive identical training, TensorRT optimization, custom kernels, buffering, and timing treatment. QuantV2X improves over CodeFilling by only 1.2/1.4 mAP30/50 in Table 3, so these details could materially affect the claimed benefit. There are no error bars or repeated-run significance analyses.

Algorithmic originality is limited: the system combines established codebook communication, block-wise reconstruction, min-max scale search, and AdaRound. The main novel element is a pair of teacher-alignment losses, but their formulation is underspecified. KL divergence is applied to feature maps without defining normalization, and the spatial loss between bounding-box representations does not explain prediction matching, confidence handling, or tensor parameterization.

Several technical definitions are erroneous or unclear. The communication-volume expressions apply a logarithm to the total byte count rather than directly computing bits/bytes. Equation 6 defines scale solely from the integer range and bit width, omitting the data range, while the calibration text reverses the stated interval as [Xmax, Xmin]. Algorithm 1 also does not clearly represent the learnable rounding variables or constraints on scale and zero-point. These may be presentation errors, but they impede verification of the method.

The claimed generality is overstated. V2X-ViT collapses from 57.4/49.5 to 29.9/8.8 under INT4/INT8, and F-Cooper also degrades substantially. Cross-dataset quantization results are limited to one main architecture. The paper should narrow its claims or develop architecture-specific treatment for attention and max-fusion models.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite the promised release. Important calibration search bounds, loss weights, quantization granularity and signedness, operator coverage, custom CUDA-kernel details, timing protocol, memory accounting, and feature-buffer policy are absent. The memory-scaling figure gives neither backbone identities nor measured memory values, making its scalability claim difficult to audit.

The broader-impact discussion focuses only on engineering benefits. Given the safety-critical autonomous-driving setting and the severe failures at 2-bit precision and on V2X-ViT, the paper should discuss failure detection, hardware-dependent numerical behavior, communication outages, and the risks of deploying quantized perception without validated safety margins. Overall, the systems direction is valuable, but these evidentiary and specification gaps produce a slight preference for rejection.

The paper addresses an important practical problem: cooperative-perception research often overlooks inference, communication, memory, and energy costs. Jointly considering model-side and communication-side efficiency is worthwhile.

The empirical scope is broader than usual: DAIR-V2X, V2X-Real, OPV2V, and V2X-ReaLO are considered; multiple fusion architectures are tested; and the appendices include calibration, bit-width, codebook, distance, pose-noise, power, and online-mode studies.

The reported model-level results are promising. INT4-weight/INT8-activation QuantV2X reaches 74.2/66.7 AP30/50 versus 75.1/68.2 in full precision on the principal DAIR-V2X setting, while the alignment losses particularly improve stricter AP70 and long-range results.

The decomposition into model-only, communication-only, and combined optimization is conceptually useful, and the V2X-ReaLO online results suggest that reducing latency can recover much of the gap between offline and online perception.
weaknesses: The central system-level evidence is internally inconsistent. Table 3 reports an 8.6 MB feature and defines communication delay using a 27 Mbps link plus U(0,200 ms). Transmitting 8.6 MB alone should take about 2.55 seconds, not the 286.8 ms reported in the Fig. 6 discussion. Likewise, a 0.03 MB message takes about 8.9 ms before the random delay, whose expectation is another 100 ms, yet QuantV2X communication is reported as 12.9 ms. Treating the stated MB values as Mb only creates a different unit inconsistency. Since the headline accuracy gains are obtained by converting these latency values into temporal misalignment, this directly undermines the main scientific claim.

The latency story mixes incompatible settings without adequate reconciliation. Fig. 5 gives 127.7 ms for full precision and 40.0 ms for QuantV2X, whereas Fig. 6 uses approximately 346.3 ms and 40.0 ms. Computation is profiled for only ten runs on a desktop RTX 3090, despite repeated claims about resource-constrained in-vehicle edge GPUs. The V2X-ReaLO table provides online accuracy but no corresponding per-configuration latency, network conditions, hardware specification, variance, or repeated-trial statistics.

Several core equations are incorrect or insufficiently defined. Equation 6 defines the quantization scale as (q_max-q_min)/(2^b-1); given the paper's definition of q_min and q_max as integer bounds, this collapses to approximately one rather than using the input range. The communication-volume expressions incorrectly place log2 around the total number of bytes. KL divergence in Eq. 9 is applied to raw BEV features without defining normalization into valid distributions, while Eq. 10 compares bounding-box representations without specifying prediction matching, confidence treatment, or how variable detection sets are handled. These are not merely cosmetic omissions because they prevent faithful reproduction of the proposed calibration procedure.

Novelty is limited and somewhat overstated. The system largely combines established AdaRound/block-reconstruction PTQ, task/feature distillation losses, and a codebook communication mechanism closely related to CodeFilling. The paper does not sharply isolate what is technically new beyond this integration, and the claim of being the first fully quantized system is not supported by a systematic accounting of which operators remain in floating point. The need for custom CUDA plug-ins makes that accounting especially important.

The memory-scaling claim is inadequately substantiated. Fig. 7 shows only a small curve over nominal 4/8/12/16 GB budgets, without identifying the backbone variants, measured peak-memory values, TensorRT workspace assumptions, batch sizes, or exact accuracy/model assignment. Claims about caching more historical BEV features are also asserted without a controlled cache-size or temporal-context experiment.

Comparisons do not fully separate the proposed components from confounders. The headline +9.5 mAP30 comparison uses an uncompressed 8.6 MB full-precision baseline; the compressed full-precision baseline is substantially stronger, and CodeFilling already supplies nearly the same codebook advantage. A matched full-precision-codebook system, with identical kernels and measured end-to-end timing, is needed to establish the incremental benefit of model quantization. Statistical uncertainty is absent throughout.

Reproducibility is weak for a systems paper: the manuscript promises a future release but does not provide code, precise custom-kernel specifications, complete quantization granularity/operator coverage, communication implementation details, random seeds, or variance. Table 13 also reports 7.02 J/query for 330 W and 47.6 QPS, whereas the stated calculation gives approximately 6.93 J/query.

Overall, the practical motivation and preliminary results have merit, but the erroneous latency accounting and underspecified deployment methodology affect the paper's principal conclusion rather than peripheral presentation. Correcting these issues would require recomputing the system-level experiments and substantially expanding the reproducibility evidence; therefore the balance favors rejection.

strengths: The paper addresses an important and practically relevant gap in cooperative perception: computation, communication, and memory costs are optimized jointly rather than treating detection accuracy or message compression in isolation. Although no contribution type is declared, Applied/Systems is more appropriate than the default Algorithms/General category; under that framing, the full-stack integration and deployment evidence constitute the main contribution.

The empirical evaluation is unusually broad. It covers DAIR-V2X, V2X-Real, OPV2V, and V2X-ReaLO; heterogeneous camera/LiDAR agents; six fusion architectures; pose perturbations; multiple bit widths; communication payloads; latency decomposition; power consumption; and GPU-memory scaling.

The core results are promising: INT4-weight/INT8-activation Pyramid Fusion retains 74.2/66.7 AP30/50 versus 75.1/68.2 in FP32 on DAIR-V2X, while the deployed INT8 configuration reduces the reported local, transmission, and fusion latency components. Online V2X-ReaLO results consistently improve over the online full-precision baseline across V2V, I2I, and V2I modes.

The component studies support the proposed design reasonably well. The heterogeneity and spatial alignment losses improve over Max-min plus AdaRound, especially at stricter IoU thresholds and longer ranges, while the codebook-size study exposes the communication–accuracy trade-off.

The manuscript is generally clear and well organized, with useful latency decompositions and a candid result showing that 2-bit quantization is currently unsuitable. The intended code release and custom TensorRT/CUDA implementation could provide substantial community value.
weaknesses: Several central deployment claims combine results obtained under different settings. The 3.2x latency result in Fig. 5 uses totals of 127.7 versus 40.0 ms, whereas the system-accuracy analysis later reports 346.3 ms for the baseline and introduces an additional U(0,200) ms asynchronous delay. Meanwhile, latency is averaged over only ten RTX 3090 runs, despite the emphasis on resource-constrained in-vehicle hardware. The paper should clearly separate measured latency from simulated delay, report variance and measurement protocol, and avoid presenting the latency and +9.5 mAP gains as though they arose from one controlled comparison.

The communication-size equations appear technically incorrect: the FP32 payload should scale as H*W*C*32 bits rather than log2(H*W*C*32/8), and the code-index payload should analogously be H*W*nR*ceil(log2(nL)) bits. The reported message sizes may nevertheless be correct, but their derivation must be fixed and verified.

Important method definitions are underspecified or questionable. Equation 6 does not give the usual data-dependent scale (x_max-x_min)/(2^b-1), the text reverses the interval as [X_max,X_min], and KL divergence is applied directly to signed BEV feature tensors without explaining normalization into valid distributions. The spatial loss likewise does not specify box matching, parameterization, or loss weights. Algorithm 1 omits several details needed to reproduce these objectives.

The claimed generalization across fusion methods is overstated. V2X-ViT drops from 57.4/49.5 to 40.0/11.0 at INT8 and 29.9/8.8 at INT4/INT8, while F-Cooper also loses appreciable accuracy. The method is convincing for Pyramid Fusion and some CNN/computation-based architectures, but not generally robust to attention-based fusion.

The algorithmic novelty is moderate: codebook communication follows CodeFilling, while scale search, adaptive rounding, and block reconstruction build heavily on established PTQ techniques. The alignment objectives and system integration are useful, but stronger controlled comparisons against BRECQ-like reconstruction, LiDAR-PTQ, and CodeFilling under identical training, hardware, and latency conditions would better isolate the new contribution.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the release promise. The manuscript lacks a concrete artifact link and omits calibration-search bounds, loss coefficients, quantization granularity, agent-sampling details, CUDA plug-in specifications, warm-up/batching settings, and repeated-run or multi-seed uncertainty. The scaling claim in Fig. 7 is also supported by only a small plot without backbone identities, measured memory footprints, or a numerical table.

As a safety-critical applied system, the paper would benefit from a substantive limitations analysis covering unsupported operators and hardware, adverse network conditions, calibration/domain shift, rare-object failures, and the accuracy consequences of stale or corrupted messages. V2X-ReaLO appears to be ROS-bag online replay rather than a live cellular-V2X testbed, so repeated descriptions of the evaluation as real-world deployment should be qualified.
